result.note: Tested the India-UK CETA entry into force, the DGFT ban on forced-labour imports, and the US Senate bill on buyers of Russian energy; skipped the unsigned India-US framework.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, which took effect in July 2026:
items: On entry into force, India eliminated duties on 96.8% of its tariff lines.
Dairy and grains were left out of the immediate duty cuts.
The Double Contribution Convention exempts roughly 75,000 Indian professionals from UK National Insurance for five years.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong. Britain scrapped duties on 96.8% of tariff lines, while India cut duties on 64.1% at once. The agreement took effect a year after signing, and TBB notes that the services surplus of nearly USD 8 billion matters more than the USD 1.76 billion goods surplus.
questions.source: The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement took effect a year after signing, with Britain scrapping duties on 96.8% of tariff lines and India on 64.1% at once, dairy and grains untouched.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, India prohibited imports made wholly or partly with forced labour. Consider the following pairs relating to this decision:
items: Body that issued the prohibition — Directorate General of Foreign Trade
Source of the wording used to define forced labour — International Labour Organization's 1930 convention
Tariff the USTR had proposed over India's failure to block such goods — 25%
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The third pair is wrong. The USTR had proposed a 12.5% tariff five weeks before India's move. No goods are being stopped at the border yet, because inquiries must first name specific products.
questions.source: India's Directorate General of Foreign Trade prohibited imports made wholly or partly with forced labour, borrowing the International Labour Organization's 1930 convention wording, five weeks after the USTR proposed a 12.5% tariff over India's failure to block such goods.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, a bipartisan US Senate bill would allow the US President to impose tariffs on the five largest buyers of Russian energy. What is the maximum tariff level the bill provides for?
questions.explain: The bill lowers the earlier ceiling of 500% to 100%. India ranks second only to China among buyers after its Russian oil imports reached a record USD 5.2 billion in June 2026, up 34%.
questions.source: A bipartisan Senate bill would let Trump impose tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian energy, with India second only to China after its Russian oil imports hit a record USD 5.2 billion in June, up 34%.
